title: Client pipeline windowing causes SSE final-block loss on resume behind aggressive proxy
text:
Client pipeline windowing causes SSE final-block loss on resume behind aggressive proxy

description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after a short network blip and automatic SSE resume, the final 'end' object for long responses is missing or truncated. This manifests as client-side hanging and incomplete final paragraphs.

Impact:
- Affects a single dedicated customer (QuillAI) using the Streaming Chat endpoint in prod-us-west.
- ~40% of resumed sessions for responses > 1,500 tokens are observed to miss the terminal 'end' block, leading to partial outputs and retries.
- Customer reports increased API error rates and user-facing truncations during a promotional burst.

Environment:
- Customer: QuillAI (dedicated)
- SDK: web-js v1.8.2 and custom Python client behind company firewall
- Network path: client -> corporate proxy -> internet -> Redwood edge (us-west) -> serving runtime
- Models: redwood-2.7b and gptj-6b variants pinned at specific versions

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use a long prompt that produces >1,500 token output.
2) Start an SSE streaming request from a client behind an aggressive corporate proxy that closes idle TCP connections after ~30s.
3) Induce a brief network disruption (simulate NAT/idle timeout) and allow client SDK to attempt resume.
4) Observe client logs and final assembly of stream; often the final JSON object with 'type': 'end' is not received.

Observed behavior:
- Client receives streaming chunks up to near-completion, then after resume sees either nothing (hang) or a truncated final chunk missing trailing newlines and the 'end' boundary.
- Server-side logs show the request finished and the runtime emitted the terminal event; the edge logs show a resume sequence where the second session gets only body fragments.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should stitch streams and deliver the terminal 'end' event intact so clients can finalize message assembly.

Attachments:
- Customer provided network capture (pcap), client SDK logs, and a short repro script. Links uploaded to the ticket.

Notes:
- Customer reproduced against our staging edge with similar proxy settings and saw the same behavior.
- Client SDK uses simple 'last-event-id' resume and replays; however their proxy performs HTTP/1.1 connection pooling and sometimes strips trailing CRLF pairs.

comments:
2026-03-10 11:05 - Customer (James Park): "We're seeing about 35% of resumed sessions drop the trailing finalization. Users get partial paragraphs. This started after our internal firewall rules tightened."
2026-03-10 12:02 - Support (Asha Patel): "Thanks James — we've escalated to infra and are collecting edge logs. Can you share SDK version and a pcap?"
2026-03-10 13:40 - Infra (Miguel Rivera): "Edge trace shows two different connection IDs for the same session token with resume offset 1.5M. The second connection appears to see fewer bytes; suspected mid-stream gateway reassembly issue."
2026-03-10 15:10 - Support (Asha Patel): "Working hypothesis: intermediate corporate proxy collapses trailing CRLF which our resume parser relies on to detect boundary; when CRLF stripped, boundary parse fails and last JSON chunk is ignored."
2026-03-11 09:22 - Customer (James Park): "We confirmed our proxy does aggressive http buffering and trims end-of-stream whitespace. Attaching proxy config snippet."
2026-03-11 11:05 - Eng (Sofia Chen): "Reproduced locally by inserting a proxy that trims CRLF on idle close. Observed identical truncated final chunk. Patch candidate: make resume parser tolerant to missing CRLF and accept end-object heuristics based on JSON completeness and boundary tokens."

investigation_notes:
Checked edge NGINX logs: saw connection goaway and new connection with X-Resume-ID header within 2s. Total bytes emitted by runtime match expected output length.
Edge reported bytes delivered on second connection smaller by 36 bytes in multiple reproductions — correlates with typical CRLF size plus final newline metadata.
Client-side SDK 'last-event-id' resume not sending explicit length; parser expects delimiting newline sequence. When stripped, downstream JSON decoder raises EOFError and client drops final object.
Tried reproducing with HTTP/2 multiplexing on client -> edge; behavior differs (no loss), indicating issue likely at HTTP/1.1 proxy reassembly path.
Captured pcap: final TCP segments show RST or FIN from proxy, and subsequent new connection omits final CRLF pair.
Related prior tickets SUP-4721 and SUP-20347 show similar resume boundary classes but different root causes (proxy chunking vs gzip mismatch).

resolution_notes:
Workaround provided to customer (2026-03-11): increase client SDK timeout to 90s and enable a post-resume 'finalize' polling call to fetch any missing tail tokens; customer accepted temporary measure.
Applied quick patch to streaming parser on edge (rollback-safe): treat a close or resume sequence as possible end boundary and attempt JSON reassembly without strict CRLF requirement. Deployed to canary edge (us-west) 2026-03-12 03:30Z.
Canary monitoring (2026-03-12): resumed sessions with proxy trimming show 98% success rate for terminal assembly (improved from 62%). No regressions observed in HTTP/2 paths.
Planned long-term fix: update resume protocol to include a terminal-checksum token embedded in final chunk metadata so future resume doesn't rely on transport-level trailing bytes. Tracking epic in INT-330 for protocol changes.
Follow-ups: update client SDK to perform an explicit 'resume-complete' handshake and document proxy requirements in the Streaming runbook.
